newsitem.title: UKRAINE: New Ukraine stand-by could be $750 mln-spokesman.
newsitem.headline: New Ukraine stand-by could be $750 mln-spokesman.

text.p: The maximum value of an International Monetary Fund interim stand-by credit to Ukraine would be $750 million, the deputy head of President Leonid Kuchma's administration said on Wednesday.
"We are talking about a one-year stand-by credit, for the last half of this year and first half of next year, whose maximum amount would be $750 million," Anatoly Halchynsky told a news conference.

An IMF mission is in Kiev this week to discuss the credit to be issued until Ukraine fulfils 41 conditions to qualify for a long-term Extended Fund Facility (EFF) of $2.5-3 billion, aimed at implementing deep structural reforms in the economy.
"At this time the government is preparing a draft memorandum project" for the stand-by, Halchynsky said. "We hope this memorandum will be confirmed."
He said Ukraine would be required to meet 32 conditions listed in the IMF-prepared memorandum while it was receiving the stand-by, but added Ukraine was negotiating some of the points.
Halchynsky said he was confident Ukraine and the IMF would reach agreement this week.
The IMF said previously the stand-by credit could be in place by the end of next month, and the EFF could be delivered late this year or early in 1998.

The two sides had originally been negotiating for the EFF, but the IMF decided to grant the stand-by credit until Ukraine met several more of the 41 conditions such as implementing changes to the tax system.
Ukraine's most recent stand-by agreement of $867 million expired in February.
